message.text: The budget measures each check's local `Finding.toJSON()` bytes, but check records serialize static sightings through `ReviewRecords.sighting`, which replaces their message and explanation with different fixed text. That projection can be larger and also erases the abridgement that `fit` measured.

evidence.snippet: export const withheld = "Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold";

## Decision

- `ReviewRecords` rewrites every static finding a record holds, in a check's or a lens's sightings and a dismissal's, Biome and tsc included. Core's `staticFindings` gives those two a fixed sentence now, but a build from before [issue #281](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/281) stored their text, and the check's name says nothing of which build wrote a sighting. Melian's round two found the first form, which left Biome and tsc alone by their check's name, trusting a label. Any static check, one Melian adds later included, is rewritten: the rule denies by default.
- A rewritten finding's message and `explanation.what` read "`<check>` reports `<rule>` here.", then the fixed sentence `withheld`. Its `whyHere` and `whatToDo` are `withheld`. It keeps its rule, place, snippet, trigger and ID, which are the head's own content. Core's `Finding.parse` takes the ID from path, rule, snippet and discriminator, never from the message, so the rewritten finding still parses with its ID.
- A finding of a tool other than Biome and tsc with no code to go by takes `message <sha256 of the tool's message>` as its discriminator, in core's `identify`. A hash is the first kind of string a record may hold. Two results of one rule with different messages keep distinct IDs, identical ones still merge into one, counted, and a repeat review of the same head gives the same IDs. Biome and tsc keep their place, `line L, column C`.
- An Enola rule ID is kept only when it is the name of one of Enola's built-in checks, or exactly the `id` of a rule the base's policy declares, in `enola/constraints/` or `enola-intent.yaml`. Any other becomes `rule-<first 16 hex of its sha256>`, so `enola/rule-<hash>` in the finding, and the rule Enola wrote moves into the local message, which the export withholds. Problem: a rule ID is also the tool's text. The rewritten sentence and the record's `ruleId` both carried it, and the rule feeds the finding's ID, so the export cannot rewrite it alone. Solution: ask the authority. [cut at 2 KiB]

explanation.what: The budget measures each check's local `Finding.toJSON()` bytes, but check records serialize static sightings through `ReviewRecords.sighting`, which replaces their message and explanation with different fixed text. That projection can be larger and also erases the abridgement that `fit` measured.
explanation.whatToDo: Measure and fit the exact shared sighting representation used by `ReviewRecords.check` (or build and size the complete check record), while still applying the corresponding abridgement to the local findings before adjudication.
explanation.whyHere: A static check can pass `fit` and complete/adjudicate as `ran`, yet its actual shared check record can still exceed `recordLimit` and be rejected during export—the failure this change is intended to close.

properties.failureScenario: Let `static.enola` return thousands of accepted findings from a declared constraint with one-character messages, enough that their local JSON is near 4 MiB. `fit` measures/abridges those short local explanations and returns an array under `recordLimit - 4096`. When `ReviewRecords.check` serializes it, every static sighting is rewritten to the longer fixed `static.enola reports ...` message and two copies of the 82-byte withheld sentence; the abridged explanation is overwritten. The resulting record exceeds 4 MiB, `MemoryRecordStore.add`/the git store rejects it as `invalidRecord`, and export fails after the check and verdict already completed.

message.text: `abridged` chooses between What and the headline by their raw UTF-8 length, although the budget bounds canonical JSON bytes. Quotes, backslashes, and control characters expand when JSON-escaped, so the chosen raw-shorter string can be the larger stored string.

evidence.snippet:
## Choice

- Past the limit, the guardrails check leaves out the detail of its last findings in ID order, as `SightingBudget.checkRecord.fit` does. A trimmed finding keeps its ID, rule, severity, resolution, place and What to do, so what blocks is unchanged. Its Why here names how many files lost their detail and says that `git diff` shows them. A finding that trimming would not make smaller keeps its detail.
- A record that still passes the limit with every finding trimmed fails the guardrails check, with `RecordError` `recordTooLarge` and a fixed sentence that holds no finding's text. The review reads not reviewed, and its records export.
- Every check's record gets the same budget, not the guardrails alone. A static tool may write 16 MiB of output, so enough Biome, tsc or Enola findings could pass the limit after adjudication had stored a verdict; `runCheck` fits every check's findings where it forms the outcome. This extension is the builder's, from Codex's adversarial review; it is not a ruling.
- The trim applies to the check's own findings, not only to the exported record. The verdict's fingerprint hashes the findings' text, so trimming at export alone would give the local and the shared verdict different texts for one round.

explanation.what: `abridged` chooses between What and the headline by their raw UTF-8 length, although the budget bounds canonical JSON bytes. Quotes, backslashes, and control characters expand when JSON-escaped, so the chosen raw-shorter string can be the larger stored string.
explanation.whatToDo: Compare the canonical JSON byte contribution of each candidate (including JSON escaping), or construct both abridged candidates and retain the one with fewer canonical bytes.
explanation.whyHere: `SightingBudget` then concludes that the finding cannot shrink and never tries the actually smaller headline. A reachable set of findings can therefore fail `recordTooLarge` even though the prescribed headline abridgement would fit the store.

properties.failureScenario: Create findings whose headline is 150 ASCII `a` characters, whose What is 149 backslashes, and whose Why here is one character. `abridged` keeps What because 149 raw bytes is less than 150, but JSON stores those backslashes as 298 bytes; choosing the headline would save 148 canonical bytes and can more than offset the fixed note. For enough such findings just over the budget, line 82 marks the chosen abridgement as non-shrinking, `fit` throws `recordTooLarge`, and the check becomes not reviewed even though replacing What with the headline would produce a storable record.

The host's local findings and terminal therefore contain only the shortened What/Why text, not the tool detail, despite the active base decision requiring every tool finding's text to remain local; the new decision has no amendment edge to that decision.

# A guardrails record fits the store, or its check fails

Status: the maintainer ruled, on [issue #605](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/605), that a guardrails record must fit the store's 4 MiB record limit, and that one which cannot fit even with every finding's detail left out fails closed. ## Problem

Every record store refuses a record past core's `recordLimit`, 4 MiB. A head that changes many workspace manifests makes one guardrails finding per manifest, each naming the scripts it changes, and their record can pass the limit. The store then refused the round's records after the harness had stored a verdict of findings, so the review threw a store error with that verdict standing.

message.text: The relay's whole-batch budget is only twice the per-record limit, but `runCheck` budgets each check independently and a round batch can contain several near-limit check records plus its account and round records.

evidence.snippet:
export const relayLimits = {
	entries: 2048,
	files: 512,
	fileBytes: recordLimit,
	bytes: 2 * recordLimit,
	extras: 64,

tiers:
  fast: [guardrails, static.biome, static.tsc, static.enola]
  # Eight repository lenses get no standards, so conventions owns them here as in full
  # (decisions/2026-11-19-lenses-get-only-the-standards-they-cite.md).
  standard: [fast, lens.correctness, lens.conventions]
  # The default full tier plus Melian's own repository lenses under .melian/lenses/. static.mutation is off this
  # repository's rounds from 2026-10-24 (decisions/2026-10-24-stryker-off-the-hot-path.md); opt in with
  # tiers: { full: [static.mutation] } in an uncommitted melian.local.yaml.
  full: [standard, lens.contracts, lens.trust-boundary, lens.trust-boundary-probes, lens.removed-behaviour, lens.tests, lens.conventions, lens.durability, lens.design]

## Decision

An Actions round shares its records only when the round closes. The round job hands the records over once `melian review` returns, and the `record` job relays them as one batch, which must hold exactly one round.

The jobs leave no other way. The round job runs the head's code, so it holds no write access to `melian/state`, as the shared-record decision's rule 9 requires. The `record` job holds that access and runs no head code, so it can start only after the round job ends. Nothing in a running round can add a batch.

A host round still adds its records in batches as its tasks finish. Only the Actions relay waits for the close.

explanation.what: The relay's whole-batch budget is only twice the per-record limit, but `runCheck` budgets each check independently and a round batch can contain several near-limit check records plus its account and round records.
explanation.whatToDo: Budget the aggregate while forming the round (failing or trimming checks until the complete batch fits), or set the relay bound from the maximum aggregate of all records a configured tier may legitimately hand over rather than assuming one full record plus one record's worth of remainder.
explanation.whyHere: The active Actions-round decision requires the completed round's records to be relayed as one batch. A large review can therefore produce only individually valid records and still have the relay refuse the entire completed round, defeating the change's intended export path.

properties.failureScenario: With the repository's `fast` tier (`guardrails`, Biome, tsc, and Enola), let three checks each produce a 2.8 MiB check record after `SightingBudget.checkRecord.fit` (for example, many manifest notices, diagnostics, and Enola findings). Every record is below the 4 MiB store limit, but the three check records alone total 8.4 MiB; the mandatory account and round add more. `RelayBatch.read` crosses `2 * recordLimit`, throws `batchTooLarge`, and the record job shares none of the completed round even though every record is storable.
